concepts.learning_objective: Find the value of a simple arithmetic expression and recognise that different expressions can have the same value.
Write an arithmetic expression that describes an everyday situation.
Compare two expressions using =, < or > according to their values.
Compare sums and differences by reasoning about how the numbers differ, without full calculation.
Use brackets to show which operation in an expression is done first.
Identify the terms of an expression by writing subtractions as additions of inverses.

topics.title: Swapping, grouping and evaluating with terms
topics.ncert_sections: 2.2 (Swapping and Grouping, More Expressions and Their Terms)

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that adding terms in any order or grouping gives the same sum.
Evaluate an expression by first evaluating each term and then adding the terms.

topics.title: Removing brackets I and tinkering the terms
topics.ncert_sections: 2.2 (Removing Brackets I, Tinker the Terms I)

concepts.learning_objective: Remove brackets correctly, changing the signs of the terms when the bracket is preceded by a minus sign.
Predict how the value of an expression changes when one of its terms is increased or decreased.

topics.title: Removing brackets II: the distributive property
topics.ncert_sections: 2.2 (Removing Brackets II, Tinker the Terms II)

concepts.learning_objective: Use the fact that a multiple of a sum or difference equals the sum or difference of the multiples.
Use the distributive property to find products quickly by splitting a number.
